summary: Lake County, OR Fremont NF steel lookout tower erected 1933 by a CCC crew; gone by 1973 per the Register and firelookout.com; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 all-steel lookout tower with a 7 x 7 steel cab
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say the tower and cabin were gone by 1973; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: manned in the 1957 and 1958 seasons and again in July 1960 (newspaper); used only for emergency fire detection by 1969

events.note: Crow's nest first (Register); an emergency lookout was staffed after lightning storms (1930 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Ground cabin (12 x 16 house and 16 x 18 garage) completed by fall 1932 as an unemployment relief project; 107-foot steel tower approved
Eight men from Camp Ingram CCC erected the 100-foot steel tower in August 1933; Register and firelookout.com date the tower to 1933
Ralph Turner returned to the lookout in July 1960 after manning it in 1957 and 1958
1969 Lookout Inventory: used only for emergency fire detection; 102-foot steel tower with 49 sq ft cab. A district memo asked that the cabin be condemned and destroyed
Civil engineer's condition survey: tower in good shape; house and garage sold but not removed
Tower and ground cabin described as gone by 1973; the sources do not say how they were removed
Registered June 10, 2011 as US 1046, OR 404; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 100 feet (1933 erection, 1959 inspection), 101 feet (Register, firelookout.com), 102 feet (1969 inventory) and 107 feet to the floor or 110 feet to the fire finder (1972 survey). The brief's 32.6 m (107 ft) was kept as the 1972 floor height.

notes_for_editor: Gone by 1973 per the Register and firelookout.com; the 1972 survey still describes the tower standing, so 'gone by 1973' is consistent. No source describes remains at the site or public access, so facts.access is omitted. Height is disputed across sources (see resolved_conflicts). Brief's coordinates and elevation (1,841 m) match the Register. Research used 1 WebSearch and about 5 page reads.
